text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — noticed a weird spike in token usage for acct rw-ops this morning. Dashboard shows several short-lived streams with full-charge entries.
Devin Patel: where are you seeing it? link: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/token-metering?range=1h
Maria Chen: timeline: client opens stream -> sends prompt -> cancels after 20 tokens -> client sees 499/backpressure -> we still log ~200 tokens charged in ledger.
Alex Rivera: that sounds like a race between stream teardown and the accounting flush. Could be in-flight batch that completes after client cancel.
Maria Chen: FYI logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-19T10:12:03Z INFO stream-session start id=ss_4c8a
2026-03-19T10:12:04Z INFO recv chunk id=ss_4c8a tokens=20
2026-03-19T10:12:04Z WARN client cancel id=ss_4c8a code=499
2026-03-19T10:12:04Z INFO batch-complete id=b_982 tokens=200 sessions=[ss_4c8a, ss_7d2b]
2026-03-19T10:12:04Z INFO billing provisional_charge id=p_112 amount_tokens=200 session_ref=ss_4c8a
```
Devin Patel: billing-bot shows provisional_charge created for each session in batch rather than prorating. @billing-bot any idea?
billing-bot: billing-service: provisional_charge created p_112 for 200 tokens (sessions: ss_4c8a, ss_7d2b). Marked provisional=true.
Alex Rivera: provisional charges are expected, but the problem is we never reconcile when the stream was canceled before the whole batch materialized. Reconciliation window looks to be 30s; these are still marked provisional after 10m.
Maria Chen: I see two potential failures: 1) session cancel not propagated to accounting shard fast enough, 2) dedupe logic for batch attribution uses session list snapshot taken before cancel and doesn't remove canceled IDs.
Devin Patel: mitigation options: - short term: extend the grace window and auto-refund if session TTL < charge tokens threshold - short-medium: change batching to mark per-session token attribution atomically when batch is completed and session is confirmed live at completion time - longer: change routing to prefer smaller batches for low-latency clients (cost tradeoff).
Alex Rivera: For the console UX, we should show provisional vs confirmed and expose "client-cancelled" flag in the token detail so folks don't have to open logs. Also add a heartbeat metric: batch_attribution_latency.
Maria Chen: Agree. Quick patch: if session cancel timestamp < batch_complete timestamp && batch_attribution includes session, mark charge suspect and emit reconcile job.
Devin Patel: I'll put up a tiny PR to emit suspect flags in accounting when cancel seen before commit. Also adding alert on sudden delta between streaming tokens and confirmed billed tokens.
Maria Chen: Can someone add a note in the rollout playbook about the console explainers and a fallback policy so Support can handle customer queries?
Alex Rivera: I'll add a short blurb and a dashboard widget that shows "provisional suspect" counts per customer.
Maria Chen: Thanks — next steps: @Devin open PR for suspect-flag; @Alex dashboard widget; I'll follow up with a small postmortem if we find affected customers.
Devin Patel: will do, aiming for patch by EOD. :thumbsup:
Alex Rivera: adding to eng-platform backlog item EP-8732.
Maria Chen: closing loop — ticketing/alerts set, and I'll notify CS if we confirm invoice-impact.
